summary: This sermon explores how to read biblical prophecy through the lens of Jesus's two comings, using Daniel 7 as a case study. The pastor interprets the four beasts as kingdoms (Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, Rome) that God sovereignly used to prepare history for Christ's first arrival, then addresses the Antichrist and the return of Christ.
key_points: All prophecy points to the first coming of Jesus or prepares us for his second coming
Overconfidence in eschatology can distract from our mission to preach the gospel
God sovereignly works through secular kingdoms to accomplish his purposes
The spirit of the Antichrist works in every generation to deceive people
Prophecy should inspire hope, not fear
big_idea: All biblical prophecy either points to the first coming of Jesus or prepares believers for his second coming, and this truth should inspire hope rather than fear or obsessive speculation.
title: Prophecy Points
